title: What if an AI designed a world and got it wrong?
author: Axx_Plays
selftext:
Hi guys, currently I’m building a 3D Metroidvania Platformer, where you play as a robotic cat exploring strange biomes created by an AI that tried to reconstruct the human world from wrong training data.  
  
Each level mixes platforming, puzzles… and glitches like frozen deserts, wrong working doors, hybrid creatures and way more.  
My project is mostly inspired by classic platforming games I used to love when I was young like Donkey Kong 64, Super Mario 64, Spiro, Rayman and so on.  
  
My self-imposed rule for the game: EVERYTHING the player sees and hears MUST be AI-Generated. Textures, music, 3D-assets, sound effects and Animations.  
For all 3D meshes, I decided to go with [Meshy.ai](http://Meshy.ai) because even low-poly generations have become surprisingly solid and when the AI gets it wrong or distorts things, it perfectly fits in my game where the AI makes mistakes. Currently there are more than 350 Meshy assets in the game and i am far away from finishing it.   
I’ve been working on this since January this year.  
  
Here's a clip, I would love to hear your thoughts and feedback.  
[https://youtu.be/47Y3YK\_uc4Q](https://youtu.be/47Y3YK_uc4Q)  
(It’s not easy for me to show this project publicly, but I want to push myself and step out of my comfort zone lol)

comments.author: Previous_Host_9990
comments.body:
Looks really cool man, congrats!  What was your experience level with game-dev prior to starting this project? What are the most interesting mechanics in the game? What are your next steps?  
  
Also - are any aspects of this a living game (eg AI generated \*as you play\*)? I'm working on a game like that, I think it's an interesting application of AI. This looks awesome and feels like it'd be impossible for a single dev to build in 8 months without AI.

replies.author: Axx_Plays
replies.body:
Thanks :)  
before this game, i made three small games and some prototypes, mostly small 3D platformer.   
I think the most interesting mechanics are time dilation and the slider mechanic (as seen in the video)  
I really like the Metroidvania genre, where you have to backtrack and reach new parts of a familiar level.   
Throughout the game you willl learn new abilities to reach points you weren't able to reach before.   
The next few months i will focus on level design and lore. For me thats the hardest part.   
  
There won't be any implementation of AI reacting during gameplay (i am way to stupid to implement this). 

I would really like to hear/see what you are working on!

replies.author: Previous_Host_9990
replies.body:
Yeah, that is what I love about the genre - that a place you once thought was useless / mundane, when you come back it's the key to advancing. The puzzle-like aspects.

This is actually the first time I'm describing my game online, so bare with me... 

The name is Monster | Hero | Quest (MHQ). The really cool parts of late 90's and early 2000's RPG's for me were the exploration and discovery... finding a new hero to join your party, or finding a new powerful monster. Players in this game discover, evolve, breed and battle an endless universe of monsters and recruit, mate, train and quest with an endless universe of heros. 

Still very much in the prototyping phase. The monster finding / breeding mechanic is pretty cool, but the rest is still in shambles... So the first three monsters are plague titan from a fire planet, a psionic succubus from an ice planet, which I bred together to get this crazy ice / fire hybrid succubus. Also adding this wood-dragon which I just thought was one of the cooler manifestations I've seen playing around with what I've built so far. To be clear all of these were generatively created in real-time while I was playing. I do find myself just spamming monster generation and then breeding together novel stuff... so I think there's some 'fun' there. But the monetization model is strange, because the more players play, the more it hits my GCP bill (mostly using Gemini). Basically there's a ton to figure out how a game like this could actually work.

replies.author: Axx_Plays
replies.body:
this sound very cool and ambitious! I recommend to go out in communities or reddit and post every milestone. its so cool to see how people get engaged in your project :)   
I hope you will get to your goal!   
Thanks for showing your progress so far

comments.author: Pentanubis
comments.body: Artificial code generation cannot get anything wrong.  You may not like the outcome but it’s 100% the right mathematical, stochastic outcome.  You asked a randomized to produce and it did.  Enjoy!

comments.author: arivanter
comments.body: I’m not gonna congratulate you on accumulating slop to create more slop but I will commend you for being straightforward with us and telling from the start that you accumulated as much slop as you could and not added anything on top.

comments.author: dragonboltz
comments.body: Awesome concept! Can't wait to see the full game

comments.author: icekiller333
comments.body:
Took a look at the trailer :) looks like a fun project - i hope you're enjoying the process.

Love the art style and the look and feel of the world, it reminds me a lot of some games i played in the 2000s. 

Sorry that people are being mean in the comments, I feel like the term slop is unjustly being assigned to things that people put real care and effort into just because it uses AI.

comments.author: Faceornotface
comments.body: People are dumb about ai. Your cake looks much better than plenty of games (which buy and use totally unoriginal assets). Not my bag but you do you - where are the enemies, tho? Did I just miss them?

replies.author: Axx_Plays
replies.body:
Thanks for your kind words.  
you didn't miss them, they are still not implemented. One Enemy, a robotic fish, is in the forest where you jump over the logs. The Game is still about 20% done
